The Parliamentary Support Network and allied civil society organisations have commended the Group Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, Bashir Bayo Ojulari, for the company’s reported financial performance and the introduction of a ₦66-per-litre discount on petrol. The groups also urged Ojulari to sustain reforms in the oil and gas sector, particularly in production growth, cost management, gas commercialisation and transparent governance. They made the call during a press conference on Friday in Abuja, where they assessed the implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act and the impact of recent initiatives by the national oil company. A copy of the address, jointly signed by Muhammad Abdulrazaq and Adams Umoren on behalf of the Parliamentary Support Network, in collaboration with the Reformers Network, was made available to PUNCH Online. According to the organisations, NNPCL’s 2025 audited financial statements, presented to President Bola Tinubu, showed a profit after tax of ₦7.2tn, representing a 33 per cent increase over the previous year. They also cited dividends of ₦5.8tn, increased remittances to the Federation Account and crude oil and condensate production of 1.77 million barrels per day, which they described as a five-year high. It added, “We gather not merely to mark another public engagement, but to reflect on a decisive chapter in Nigeria’s petroleum history—one defined by the bold vision of the Petroleum Industry Act and the determined leadership that is translating that vision into measurable results for the ordinary Nigerian.” The organisations noted that the industry had faced volatile global oil prices, changes arising from downstream deregulation and persistent infrastructure challenges. SERAP sues INEC over N126bn electoral funds Tinubu committed to LG autonomy — Uzodimma Let Oyebanji govern, Tinubu cautions succession hopefuls “Yet under Ojulari’s leadership, NNPC demonstrated resilience by focusing on operational efficiency, cost discipline, and production recovery,” the statement said. The groups also highlighted the company’s ₦66-per-litre petrol discount at its retail stations, introduced to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary and extended until the end of October. They said the initiative was funded from NNPCL’s retail margin rather than the Federation Account, describing it as a corporate responsibility measure intended to provide relief to motorists, transport operators and households amid rising living costs. “The initiative is funded from the company’s own retail margin—not from the Federation Account. It is not a return to the old subsidy regime,” the statement said. “It is a deliberate act of corporate responsibility that prioritises relief for motorists, transporters, and households struggling with the cost of living.” The organisations further pointed to progress on critical gas infrastructure, including the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano pipeline, saying such projects could support industrial growth and improve power supply. While acknowledging the challenges associated with transforming the oil and gas sector, the groups maintained that the reforms being pursued under Ojulari were moving in the right direction. “We recognise that no reform is without challenges. Legacy issues, global market volatility, and the sheer scale of transforming a decades-old institution will continue to test resolve,” the statement said. “Yet the Parliamentary Support Network believes that the direction of travel under Engr. Ojulari is the right one. The PIA provided the legal and institutional framework.
